page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. It provides 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI are supported, alongside vector instructions including standard AVX, though AVX-512 extensions are absent.

The server is provisioned with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via 1200 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing low-latency disk I/O without relying solely on networked block storage. The platform delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware acceleration via dedicated GPUs is not present on this server configuration.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded performance alongside lower single-core execution speed. Stress-ng single-core performance registers in the bottom 10% (767.99), whereas multi-core stress-ng reaches an average tier of 12291.87. Geekbench results follow a similar pattern with a single-core score of 1324.0 and a multi-core score of 11582.0. Memory subsystem testing shows robust bandwidth, reaching 70.1 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and a strong PassMark memory score of 2816.88. In CPU workloads, PassMark yields 34594.3 overall, with 34141.18 in cryptographic operations.

The c5ad.8xlarge provides a cost-efficient profile for organizations requiring high core counts coupled with high-speed local disk capacity. The integrated 1200 GB NVMe SSD volume avoids additional networked storage overhead for temporary scratch space. However, workloads requiring heavy AVX-512 acceleration or strong single-thread throughput may find the AMD Zen 2 architecture limiting.

The instance is well suited for distributed build systems, Clang software compilation, multi-threaded batch data processing, media transcoding, and caching layers like Redis. It also functions effectively as a compute worker for data manipulation and ETL pipelines that benefit from fast local temporary scratch storage.
